key_insight: Disentangling pose from shape and conditioning retrieval on estimated camera pose lets a model map occluded single views into a pose-normalized 3D shape space, yielding more robust and interpretable 3D retrieval from partial observations.
problem_solved: How to reliably retrieve the correct 3D shape from a single, often heavily occluded view where holistic image–shape alignments fail due to viewpoint and missing-visible-part ambiguities.
method: Pose-aware decomposition: estimate camera pose from the input view and use it to canonicalize or condition downstream shape embeddings.

Occlusion-robust shape encoder: train a shape embedding that aligns partial (occluded) views with full 3D shapes using pose-conditioning and contrastive/retrieval objectives with synthetic occlusion augmentation.
Pose-conditioned retrieval and attention to visible regions to improve interpretability and reduce false matches caused by occluders or extreme viewpoints.
impact: Makes single-view 3D retrieval practical in real-world settings (robotics, AR, inventory search) by improving robustness to occlusion and viewpoint changes and by producing more interpretable embeddings for debugging and downstream use.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: occluded input image → pose estimator → pose-normalizer/conditioner → shape encoder → retrieval results.
Before/after examples: retrieval failures of a holistic baseline vs correct matches from the pose-aware approach on occluded inputs.
Canonicalization visualization: partial input transformed to a canonical pose alongside the retrieved 3D model to show alignment.
Embedding-space plot (t-SNE/UMAP) highlighting separation of shapes when conditioned on pose and showing clustered occluded vs full-view embeddings.
paper_title: PASR: Pose-Aware 3D Shape Retrieval from Occluded Single Views
paper_authors: Jiaxin Shi, Guofeng Zhang, Wufei Ma, Naifu Liang, Adam Kortylewski
